summary: A note from Robert Kahn about a computer communication network demonstration he was organizing for the International Computer Communications Conference in Washington on 24 to 26 October 1972. The demonstration would run alongside the conference sessions and show network use.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC describes plans for a computer network demonstration at the International Computer Communications Conference. A TIP at the conference hotel would let visitors use selected network resources from terminals.

questions: what was planned for the iccc network demonstration
subtitle: A plan for hands-on network demonstrations at the October 1972 ICCC.

tldr.problem: Conference attendees needed a way to experience computer networking directly and see examples of its use.
tldr.mechanism: The plan is to connect a TIP at the Washington Hilton to the ARPANET and let conference terminals access selected network resources.
tldr.outcome: The RFC asks network sites to help prepare resources and clear documentation for people new to the network.

sections.title: The Conference Demonstration
sections.content:
The International Computer Communications Conference is scheduled for October 24 to 26, 1972, at the Washington, D.C. Hilton Hotel. Robert Kahn is organizing a network demonstration to run alongside the conference sessions.

The demonstration is intended to give attendees first-hand experience using a computer network.
sections.plainLanguage: The conference includes a live network demonstration at the Hilton. Visitors are meant to try a network themselves, not only hear about it.

sections.title: Resources Available to Visitors
sections.content:
The demonstration will emphasize database retrieval, combining several machines, real-time data access, interactive cooperation, simulation systems and simplified hard copy techniques. The plan is to install a TIP at the Hilton and connect it to the ARPANET.

Terminals at the Hilton will connect to the TIP. ARPANET resources and resources in other networks that can be temporarily connected may be made available.
sections.plainLanguage: Visitors would use terminals connected to a TIP to reach selected computer resources. The RFC lists several kinds of activity the demonstration hopes to show.

sections.title: Preparation and Requests for Help
sections.content:
The organizers and the NIC are preparing explicit documentation in accessible terms so inexperienced users can use selected resources without assistance. The author describes this as a substantial task and asks network sites to contribute time and effort.

Robert Kahn invites suggestions and requests for information about the demonstration.
sections.plainLanguage: Clear instructions are needed so visitors who have not used a network can participate. The organizer asks sites in the network community to help prepare the event.
